Subject: Renewal planning — commit increase and rate limits

Hi Jasmine,

We're starting renewal discussions for our hosted API account. Usage has ramped faster than the forecasted curve — November showed a 48% month-over-month token increase and we hit the burst window twice. We want to increase our monthly commit and also understand how rate limits will change for higher tiers.

High-level ask: can Redwood propose an amendment that increases our monthly commit from 1.2B tokens to 2.5B tokens, clarifies per-request concurrency limits, and documents fallback behavior (e.g., quota throttling vs queued requests) during heavy traffic? Procurement would like a draft amendment and a sample SLA paragraph for latency targets for the renewed term.

I'm attaching our November usage snapshot. Happy to hop on a call next week — mornings PST are best.

Thanks,
Samantha

Subject: Draft amendment and rate-tier proposal (v1)

Hi Samantha — attaching a first-pass amendment and a compact summary of rate tiers for the 2.5B commit you requested. Highlights:
- Monthly commit: 2.5B tokens (12-month term)
- Unit pricing bands (hosted): 0–500M, 500M–2.5B with stepped price reductions at 1.25B
- Rate limits: default per-account concurrency 40 req/s; per-route spiky allowance configurable up to 120 req/s with negotiated burst window
- Fallbacks: when commit capacity is exhausted, requests are queued for up to 15s; customers can opt into auto-fallback to lower-cost model variants for best-effort reliability

I've kept the amendment language minimal to speed legal review. Two outstanding items I flagged: (1) explicit latency SLOs tied to p95 and model family, (2) a clause for annual usage true-up.

Hi Samantha and team — quick clarifications inline below: 

1) Queueing behavior: the 15s queue reference is at the Redwood hosted control plane/runtime boundary — requests are accepted at regional edge, and in the event of transient capacity pressure we apply orderly queuing with regional fallbacks. For cross-region traffic we recommend pinning a primary region for low-jitter behavior.

2) Burst credit / cost cap: we can add a negotiated burst-credit bucket (example: 200M tokens of burst credits per quarter) and an overage cap that triggers a manual notification and pause threshold. We will propose the exact numbers in v2 of the amendment.

3) SOC2 and evidence: Redwood will include SOC2 Type II support in the enterprise addendum and a 12-month evidence retention clause for required logs. We'll include the SOC2 download link and a sample audit response timeline.

I've updated the internal checklist and will fold the procurement language into v2. If helpful, Marissa can join the call to confirm SLA language.

Neha
